Motion demonstrates Galbot S1 palletizing at Slush and outlines Belgian delivery

A Helsinki event report documents crate stacking alongside leasing, operator training and remote-support details.

Robotics Norway ↗19 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 6Videos 1

Crate stacking on stage

Robotics Norway reported Motion’s Galbot S1 palletizing demonstration at the Industrial Renaissance Summit during Slush on November 19. Alexander Stevens described a 320 kg robot with a 50 kg payload and lidar-based slowing near people. These are presentation details, not blanket certification of safety in every installation.

Deployment includes support services

Motion leases robots and quoted current robot costs of €100,000–€150,000, not monthly rental prices. Its Google Cloud- and Gemini-based MotionOS covers customer-video qualification, digital-twin planning, VR training and fleet management. The company described camera and AR-glasses training for operators and remote teleoperation support.

A planned customer shipment

Stevens said the demonstration robot would ship to a Belgian warehouse customer the following week, and that customer numbers grew from six to 50 within two months of its pre-seed announcement. Shipment was still prospective at the time of reporting. Event photos and video show the stage demonstration, not sustained customer-site performance or warehouse investment returns.
